static_traits.name: Chen Bowen
static_traits.social_status: Interpersonal relationships affected by fear of being judged, avoiding talking about hobbies in social gatherings; has several close friends but has not yet discussed these feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of psychotherapy; not yet had similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and coherently, capable of self-reflection and cooperation; neutral tone, can describe specific social events, presenting anxiety and self-doubt

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling that liking reading and <Ender's Game> makes others see oneself as 'pretentious' in social settings, thus developing intense self-consciousness and doubt; feeling anxious when talking about hobbies, and avoiding related topics.
basic_info.core_demands: Because excessive self-consciousness affects enjoyment of hobbies and socializing, hopes to relieve these troubles through counseling, and talk about and participate in their own interests at ease in social settings again.

core_beliefs: Expressing true interests will make others think she is pretentious
I do not fit in with others; others will look down on me because of my hobbies

special_situations.event: At a party, someone made a sarcastic comment about his liking science fiction books
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others show disapproval or mockery toward my interests, it means I am pretentious and not accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Laughing it off on the spot and quickly switching topics; afterward, avoiding talking about books and reading in social settings as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am very pretentious; talking more will get me mocked

special_situations.event: When quoting book content in conversation, someone rolls their eyes in contempt
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' impatience or contemptuous expressions mean my interests are out of place or off-putting
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Compresses self-expression; avoids sharing views and quoted content
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not talk about my hobbies

special_situations.event: Being asked about hobbies by others in social gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I talk about reading and <Ender's Game>, others will think I consider myself extraordinary and do not fit in
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding answering directly and changing to other topics to avoid negative evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Saying it will only make things awkward; they may be disdainful

special_situations.event: When the conversation topic turns to content one is not interested in
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When my interests differ from the group's, it means I do not fit in and will be excluded
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Going along with group topics, repressing self-expression to maintain superficial harmony
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I simply do not fit in

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted, to express one's interests authentically, and to gain understanding and respect
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being humiliated, mocked, or rejected; worrying about being seen as pretentious and not fitting in
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by downplaying and avoiding self-expression
Maintains superficial harmony to avoid social conflict and embarrassment

object_relations.self_representation: An outsider who is easily mocked and needs to hide oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited in social or counseling settings to share books/hobbies
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person might mock me like the people at the party did (transference: projecting past experiences of judgment onto the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopt a gentle, supportive tone; first empathize with the worries and shame, then invite descriptions of specific details with open-ended questions; allow pauses and emotional fluctuations, avoiding judgmental language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others show impatience or sarcastic nonverbal cues (e.g. rolling eyes)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views others as contemptuous judges and believes one must retreat immediately for self-protection
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a steady, low-stimulation tone; first name the on-site cues and feelings, then gently invite distinguishing the difference between facts and interpretation; encourage expressing experiences in 'I' statements.

manifestations: Worrying about being excluded by the group because of one's interests, avoiding talking about oneself socially to avoid judgment
Choosing to downplay self-expression when asked about hobbies, feeling 'not fitting in'
outcomes: Interpersonal tension, difficulty building genuine connections

manifestations: Wavers between authentic expression and catering to others, finding it hard to present oneself autonomously in socializing
Limits choices and expression to avoid judgment
outcomes: Reduced satisfaction from interests, limited experience

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worries excessively about others' opinions before socializing and is especially cautious about expressing hobbies
Tending toward self-doubt, personalizing others' reactions

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: At gatherings, laughs it off and quickly changes the topic to avoid discussing books and reading
Not answering directly when asked about hobbies, displacing to safe topics

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Assuming others will see oneself as pretentious before they have explicitly judged
Generalizes a few negative interactions into the group's view

positive_force: Sincere love of reading, which can bring positive emotions and a sense of worth
Having several close friends to get support from (though not yet discussed this distress)
Can notice and name cognitive distortions, willing to try alternative perspectives and cognitive restructuring
Proactively seeks counseling help; clear motivation to change
negative_force: Overly focuses on negative interactions; marked mental filtering
Mind reading and predicting the future causing anxiety and avoidance even before socializing
Fears being judged, tends to downplay and avoid self-expression
Excessive self-monitoring and self-doubt, prone to personalizing others' reactions

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding talking about interests in social situations, changing topics, accompanied by significant anxiety
antecedent: Being asked about hobbies by others
When Ender's Game or reading-related topics come up
Encounters sarcastic comments or cues like others rolling their eyes
target_behavior.core_reason: Intense worry about being judged and humiliated, reinforced by past negative interactions, forming catastrophizing and overgeneralization about self-expression
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential negative evaluation and embarrassment, maintaining surface safety and group harmony
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, reduced social participation, decreased enjoyment of hobbies, developing self-incongruence and persistent self-doubt
